scope: Offline functional-path qualification; no hardware calls, mutations or new control claimed.

ms.finding: Both calls reside in the same unwind-bounded function 82BBA0..82BD4E. 82BC1A invokes 771C00 with bool1; success sets local r15b. The routine performs an object operation at offset 0x214 and polls bit0. Its completion and timeout branches join at 82BD1B, which tests r15b then 82BD29 invokes 771C00 with bool0 before returning. The controller4 request is scoped to this internal operation; an external caller cannot hold it beyond that return through this path. This does not establish absence of other controls.
ms.next_requirement: A different externally callable request with an independent owned lifetime is required; tracing callers of82BBA0 cannot turn this bounded operation into a lasting hold.

native_contract.set_20801818: 8 bytes: u16 snoop value +0, u8 snoop scale +2, u16 no-snoop value +4, u8 no-snoop scale +6. Setter masks value 10 bits, scale 3 bits; no range validation in selected routine.
native_contract.request_8a254: snoop value bits10:1; snoop scale13:11; forced bit14=1; no-snoop value24:15; no-snoop scale27:25; forced bit28=1; bit0 trigger=1 and polled. Remaining retained bits follow read/modify/write mask 0xf0004001, combined with forced 0x10004001.
native_contract.get_20801817: reads 8a24c and projects snoop value9:0 scale12:10; no-snoop value23:14 scale26:24. Public output excludes status bits13 and27 and trigger-source bits. Error is suppressed by outer handler.
native_contract.relation: Shifting request fields and forced bits right by one matches the status field layout exactly; official NVIDIA GA102 published LAST_MSG_SENT uses the same status layout including requirement bits13 and27. This homologous mapping does not prove current register names, each SET reflected as latest message, requirement meaning, or ability to deassert.
native_contract.units: Pinned NVIDIA public API header gives no units or permitted scale semantics. Prior primary Linux source L1.2 threshold encoding uses scales0..5 for 1,32,1024,32768,1048576,33554432 ns; it is analogous PCIe encoding, not proof of this NVIDIA API. Scales6..7 are not rejected by selected setter; semantic validity is unestablished.
native_contract.ownership: No separate owned handle or release operation exists in public SET packet; setter issues a message trigger and returns after bit clears or timeout. Duration and replacement semantics beyond that event are not established.

zero_request_example.conclusion: Even with all four public values zero, the packed request differs from the captured all-zero raw baseline. Public GET omits these additional bits, so equality of its four fields cannot establish equality of the request.

primary_semantics.scope: Independent PCIe LTR example on Intel I210, not a binding of NVIDIA proprietary registers.
primary_semantics.paraphrase: With a requirement asserted, zero latency requests best service. Clearing the requirement denotes no latency requirement. Device-specific scale choices must not be generalized to this NVIDIA interface.

ltr.next_requirement: Bind the current NVIDIA request/status semantics and distinguish an actual reflected SET from unrelated last-message updates. No claim that unknown reset/replay behavior is a prerequisite to all other functionality.

other_scopes: ASPM and alternate NVDEC controller17 remain separately unqualified. Recovery, Undo and profile replay remain deferred. No new hardware trial was run.

vat_profiler.scope: Pinned 617.42 offline decoder audit only; no GPU operations or mutations.
findings: Current public header calls feature VAT without expanding it; profiler control bits11:10 encode ignore0, disable1 (0x400), enable2 (0x800), release3 (0xc00). B0CC0301 request packet is 12 bytes (globalStatus, controlMask, statusMask); B0CC0302 release is 4-byte controlMask. Documented request lifetime is tied to B2CC profiler object or explicit release.

Pinned Windows request handler 436730 decodes exactly five two-bit fields through 9:8; at 43688A it shifts input8 and masks3, decodes last field, then immediately calls 42EA10. It neither decodes VAT bits11:10 nor forwards them. Manager 42E305 restricts active request to 0x3ff.
Status translator 84DFA0..84E0F3 rewrites only bits0..9, leaving output status bits11:10 unchanged from caller input. They are not a VAT result and can mislead if zero initialized.

Release handler 435F80 checks five fields through mask0x300, then forwards to 42E830; VAT release bits do not reach manager. There is no selected VAT callback, current VAT capability probe or independent readback on this pinned request path. Behavior of other binaries is not inferred.

Descriptor E5C490 binds B0CC0301 size12 to wrapper 175B70 (+178), and B0CC0302 size4 to wrapper 175B80 (+180). For profiler HAL selector2, initializer 16F5CB1..CF4 assigns +178=436730 and +180=435F80; other HAL selectors can use distinct methods and are not covered by the real-handler findings.

elpg_enable_admission.scope: Offline static 617.42, no hardware or product mutation; source observations are not a universal driver guarantee.

findings.membership: Factory zeroes 0x1960 bytes. 3057e8 initializes support bitmap 0x3ffff7; 3057f2..81a invokes 736db0 only for its set bits, all below 22. 752430 adds only when 7383f0 confirms index <22 and currently supported. Three direct calls to removal helper 752480 at 739de9, 739f84, 73a0ff precede their respective support bit clears; removal clears the index in all four masks. These paths maintain membership subset of currently supported indices. Exhaustiveness of all support and membership writers is not established by this artifact.
findings.callback: 73a480 zero-count reason0 branch logs and calls +50 even if count was zero. 17e1580 selects 7377f0 if third descriptor word +10 equals 2, else 92d80 returns 0x56. 7377f0 resolves another object and, depending on its +48 low nibble and group+1958, calls e49a0 with callback 7345b0 and argument 0x258 or sets a bit in resolved+40. Thus callback is not generally equivalent to leaving all state unchanged on a zero mask. Descriptor selection for a specific runtime and e49a0 semantics are not established here.
findings.decision: Documented membership construction/update preserves selected members within supported IDs, and queued callback is policy-gated reevaluation consistent with ENABLE. However A801 type3 group support does not disclose the parallel object capability or reason bit: admission needs a qualified getter for GPU+2550 +f10 and, if active, +fc8 bit2 and +f24 semantics, or another source-proven constraint establishing the operation cannot affect an independently held request.
findings.deferred_followup: 7345b0 checks group+1958 then calls 305b00 and clears the queued flag. 305b00 iterates all supported members; 73a1f0 requires full reason mask +110 zero and state +114 nonzero before transition helpers 739620/73a5a0 and clears +114. If group+e3 set, 737b80 independently checks +11c zero and +120 before its own transition. This is a policy-gated all-supported reevaluation, not an unconditional reason0 count decrement; exact lower helper effects are not resolved. The third selector descriptor is cast from owner (fallback class 34a6d6) at 17e1f3b..f8f; its word +10 selects callback, but actual runtime value is not bound.
findings.parallel_object: Feature6 group case 42b784 requires GPU+2550+12c0, checks group0/1/3 masks and independently tests 7ec4e0(GPU+2550): +f10 >=2 and odd. If true, ENABLE/final release also calls 7ec3f0 with reason2, clears +fc8 bit2 and +f24 byte, and invokes object+130 method with state0 if resulting +fc8 is zero. A801 type3 reads the group object at +12c0 and cannot by itself exclude the parallel +f10 branch; it is not an alternative mutually exclusive group path. Current support reads do not establish +f10 or +fc8 values.
